analysis: The only change in this batch is a new test file, provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Models/StreamingFileDownloadDelegateTests.swift (lines 1-159). It adds no production code, so it creates no new attack surface or regression against TB-002 or TB-011. The tests exercise StreamingFileDownloadDelegate completion ownership. They cover cancellation before the waiter attaches, either ordering of attachment and completion, first-terminal-error-wins, preservation of the partial file on cancel, and a 100-iteration concurrent attachment race. Security-relevant behavior this touches is the model download path (A-004, T-012, T-016). The tests confirm the delegate ignores late data callbacks after completion (lines 73-75), which is a hardening property. No network contact occurs: the fixture uses the reserved .invalid domain with a suspended task. Temporary files are created under a UUID-named directory in the temp directory and removed in close(). This is test-only, with no secrets and no trust-boundary interaction. Remaining questions: the production delegate (StreamingFileDownloadDelegate and its attach and completion logic) was not supplied in this batch, so whether it actually enforces these properties is outside the evidence. Integration should check that the production change matches, and that weight integrity checks, which are not touched here, still apply to downloaded model files.
